message_1_subject: Post-call: model fit & structured-output eval next steps (FinTechCo)
message_1_body:
Hi Kate,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the payments reconciliation use case and the requirement to return deterministic JSON records for downstream ingestion. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Summary of needs: small multi-field JSON output per transaction (txn_id, status, reason_code, confidence), strict schema validation (we'll run schema compliance evals), idempotent retries for transient failures, and throughput target ~200 TPS during peak batch windows.
- Suggested model candidates for initial eval: Redwood-2-7B-quant (fast, lower cost, good for deterministic schema compliance) and Llama3-13B-q8_0 (higher quality on edge cases; higher token cost).
- Quantization / latency tradeoffs: we recommend starting with the 2.7B quantized profile to validate schema compliance and then run edge-case evals on the 13B variant for quality-sensitive paths.
- Structured output / tool calling notes: we'll use function-calling to return a validated JSON payload; our eval harness will test JSON schema compliance across the prompt set and also verify retry/duplicate suppression logic.

Attached: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (30 prompts covering happy + edge cases), eval_report_summary.pdf (initial benchmark template). Also linking our internal benchmark doc: https://drive.redwood.internal/benchmarks/fintechco-model-fit-2026

Proposed next steps:
1) I can run a 1k-query schema-compliance eval against both models by EOD Thursday (2026-02-27) and share results.
2) Can you share a short example OpenAPI / function signature for the JSON we must return? If you can drop that here or into the Drive doc, I’ll add it to the harness.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up for Wed 3/2 to review results and recommend the production profile.

Thanks — I’ll queue the eval once I have the schema.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
(415) 555-0199
message_2_subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & structured-output eval next steps (FinTechCo)
message_2_body:
Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. 

This looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- Schema: we'll expect an array of objects (max 1 per input) with fields: txn_id (string), status (enum: APPROVED, DECLINED, REVIEW), reason_code (string|null), confidence (float 0-1). I'll paste our OpenAPI snippet below for reference.
- Retries / idempotency: we need a retry strategy where the server may return a 5xx and the client will retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff. We will dedupe on txn_id. Can you confirm Redwood’s runtime will preserve deterministic outputs across retries (i.e., same prompt + same model + same seed should produce the same JSON)?
- Quality regression: we have an internal acceptance threshold of >=95% schema compliance and >=90% accuracy on label-sensitive cases (we can provide a labeled eval set). If model updates cause regressions, we need a rollback path and notification hook (webhook) for automated fallback.

OpenAPI snippet (quick paste):
---
paths:
  /predict:
    post:
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/TxnRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TxnResponse'
components:
  schemas:
    TxnResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        txn_id:
          type: string
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [APPROVED, DECLINED, REVIEW]
        reason_code:
          type: string
          nullable: true
        confidence:
          type: number
          format: float
---

We’ll upload the labeled eval set to the Drive link and give HubSpot access if needed. Also can you confirm SLAs? We’re evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted — latency SLOs of <150ms p50 and <300ms p95 for the 2.7B profile are desirable.

Thanks,
Kate
VP, Product — FinTechCo
message_3_subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & structured-output eval next steps (FinTechCo)
message_3_body:
Hi Kate — looping in Connor from Solutions so we can answer the runtime / SLA questions. Short answers: 

- Determinism / retries: Redwood’s hosted runtime supports deterministic seeds at the request level if you pass a fixed seed and use the same model + quantization profile. For retries we recommend the client dedupe by txn_id; server-side we can attach request_id and we also support idempotency keys when using our Dedicated product.
- Schema compliance: our eval harness can run JSON Schema validation (we will use your OpenAPI -> JSON Schema conversion). The eval will report per-field pass rates, common failure modes (truncation, extra fields, enum mismatches), and example prompts causing failures.
- Rollback & notifications: we support canary rollouts, automatic fallback to pinned model variants, and webhook notifications on quality regression alerts. We can wire a webhook to your endpoint to post alerts if schema compliance drops below a threshold.

I’ve kicked off a 1k-query run (both models) and will upload a preliminary CSV and a short Redgate-style eval snapshot to the Drive link. Also attaching redwood_config.yaml which shows the eval settings (batch size, retries=3, schema-check enabled). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FT-2026-0421 (I added the FinTechCo repo link).

Attachment stubs: redwood_config.yaml (config snippet), small_eval_snippet.csv (preview).

Proposed meeting: Wed 2026-03-02 at 09:00 PT (I’ll send a calendar invite).

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
